title.title: Toda's Gepner point on every quintic threefold
title.subtitle: Claim: a Bridgeland stability condition whose phases shift by exactly $2/5$ under the Gepner autoequivalence

plain: Physicists predicted a perfectly symmetric way to sort the 'branes' on a quintic shape; it exists

beats.text: A stability condition gives every stable object a phase
Apply $T_{\mathcal O} \circ (-\otimes \mathcal O(1))$: every phase moves by the same amount
The claim: exactly $2/5$, on every smooth quintic

achievement.label: Toda's Gepner conjecture (2014)
statement: T_{\mathcal O}\circ(-\otimes\mathcal O(1)) \text{ shifts phases by } \tfrac{2}{5}
achievement.context: Before: Chunyi Li built large-volume stability on the quintic (2019); the Gepner point was open
achievement.note: Also large-volume stability on every Calabi–Yau threefold

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: A Gepner point on every quintic.
Physics predicts a stability condition with a symmetry of order five.
Building any stability condition needed a Bogomolov-Gieseker-type inequality.
Claimed: Toda's Gepner point, with phases shifting by two fifths.

sources.quote: Chunyi Li (Invent. Math. 2019) for the quintic (large volume)
Toda's Gepner conjecture (Toda 2014 via matrix factorizations) open
